AN.title: make A2 decidable while the log is being written
AN.commit: fix(doctor): decide A2 against a pinned prefix, not the live tail
AN.note:
MEASURED 24 Aug 2026. A2 is not failing because replay is broken -- replay reproduces exactly. It fails because `doctor` compares the persisted projection against a replay of the *live* log, and with ~20 agents appending, events land between the two reads. Observed in one sitting, same repository, minutes apart: FAIL ('canonical state diverged'), then UNKNOWN ('state covers N of M events'), then PASS -- the last only because the rebuild and the check happened in the same instant.

So the condition as written is decidable only on a quiet repository, and this repository is never quiet. A gate that reports three different verdicts for one unchanged history is measuring contention, not replay.

Fix it by deciding A2 against a **pinned prefix**: take the projection's own high-water mark, replay exactly that many events, and compare. Events appended after the mark are outside the comparison -- they are not evidence of divergence and must not be reported as such. A genuine mismatch inside the prefix must still FAIL, and an empty prefix must still be UNKNOWN (do not reintroduce the tautological pass repaired on 20 Aug 2026).

The test is the point of this unit: `tests/test_doctor_a2_concurrent.py` must append to the log *while* the check runs and assert the verdict is stable and correct. A test that only runs on a quiet log reproduces the bug it is meant to catch.

Do NOT make A2 pass by widening what counts as identical. The divergence report is right in principle; the read window is what is wrong.

AO.title: record the 22 August capture loss as baseline, once torn appends are refused
AO.commit: docs(adr): baseline the 22 August capture loss, contingent on AB
AO.note:
DECIDED by Joe, 24 Aug 2026. MEASURED same day: A3 is permanently unpassable as written. `pass` requires `run >= 7 AND new_refused == 0`. `run_start` walks backwards through consecutive capture days; 19-24 August are consecutive with no gap; three lines on 2026-08-22 (offsets 27, 35, 45) are invalid JSON, written by something that bypassed `append()`. Because the run never slides forward while capture continues daily, those three stay inside the window forever. The only way the current code passes is to STOP CAPTURING for a day, which resets run_start past the 22nd -- a capture gate you pass by breaking capture.

Write ADR-0105 recording those three digests as a known, permanent loss, exactly as ADR-0043 did for the original three, and add them to HISTORICAL_REFUSAL_DIGESTS. A3 then measures NEW loss going forward, which is what it is for.

**This unit must not land before AB.** AB makes a torn append refuse and name its offset. Baselining a loss whose cause is still live turns A3 into a ratchet that absorbs every future corruption and detects nothing -- that is the objection Joe was shown and the reason for the dependency. State it plainly in the ADR's 'evidence against' section, along with the rule: the baseline may only ever absorb a loss whose cause has been fixed and whose fix has shipped.

Do NOT widen A3, change its arithmetic, or make it a trailing window. The condition is right; the history under it is damaged.

AP.title: Gate B4: real upstream work on pytest, verified by pytest's own suite

AP.note:
DECIDED by the principal, 24 August 2026: Gate B4's twenty tickets must be REAL, VALUABLE upstream work on an open-source project we actually depend on -- not an arbitrary corpus.

THE CORPUS. `pytest-dev/pytest` is cloned at C:/Users/jpbpr/Repositories/pytest-upstream, MIT licensed, allowlisted under ADR-0063, with an ISOLATED VENV at .venv already installed editable. Verified 24 Aug: `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest testing/test_mark.py -q` gives 118 passed, and Consilient's own interpreter still resolves the system pytest, so the two environments do not collide. ALWAYS use that venv's interpreter for corpus work; using the system python runs the tests against the WRONG pytest and the import error is confusing.

Why pytest: it is in this project's own dev dependencies, we run it hundreds of times a day, and we hold MEASURED expertise in a defect class it carries -- on 24 Aug we established that `taskkill /T /F` is not atomic with a deadline (a 1s timeout returned at 1.91s and a grandchild acting at 1.5s escaped every attempt) and fixed it with a Windows Job Object in scripts/proc_tree.py. Windows process handling is a genuine, evidenced contribution area for us.

WHAT COUNTS. Read `_foreign_tickets` in src/consilient/cli.py before writing anything; it defines admission and most of this unit is conforming to it. Per ticket the trajectory needs an `attempt.outcome` carrying that repository, `verifier_accept: true` and a task or attempt_id, PLUS a matching `ticket.completed`. Both must go through `append()`. A line written directly to the file does not count, by design.

QUALITY IS THE POINT, NOT THE COUNT. Twenty low-value diffs on a major open-source project would be worse than zero: it wastes maintainer attention and it would embarrass the principal. So: find work from the project's OWN open issues and its own stated priorities -- do not invent tasks to hit a number. Each ticket must be defensible to a pytest maintainer on its merits. A change whose test cannot fail has produced nothing; if you can delete the assertion and the suite stays green, that is a finding, not a ticket.

SCOPE OF THIS UNIT: the runner plus THREE genuine tickets end to end, proving `consil doctor` moves B4 from 0 to 3. Do not attempt twenty here. Report what you found and what you judged not worth doing -- the refusals are as valuable as the completions.

Do NOT open pull requests. Producing the verified work is this unit; submitting anything upstream is the principal's decision and his alone.

AQ.title: release the claims of a dispatch that never started
AQ.commit: fix(coordination): release claims held by a run that never started
AQ.note:
MEASURED 24 Aug 2026. N00 gave us detection: the driver reports START_FAILED when a run writes no artefact inside the start window. Nothing releases what that run claimed, so its paths stay locked for the full hour. Observed in one tick: two dispatches died at startup (0 bytes after 509s and 432s) and their claims then refused T01 and AA -- T01 being the unit that gates 22 others. The hour was spent twice over on runs that were never alive.

`close_claim(log, run_id=...)` already exists and is properly attributed to DISPATCH_ACTOR; `live_claims` already treats a terminal dispatch event as a release. The missing half is calling it.

**The hazard is the whole of this unit.** Releasing the claim of a run that is merely SLOW, rather than dead, admits two agents to one path -- exactly what the claim exists to prevent, and a far worse outcome than an hour's delay. So a release must be justified by evidence the process is gone, not by absence of an artefact. Establish liveness properly: map the run to its process and confirm it is not running, and refuse to release when liveness cannot be determined. Fail closed.

Do NOT shorten the claim expiry to paper over this, and do NOT release on artefact silence alone. A silent process holding a lock and a dead one look identical from the artefact; that is the whole difficulty and the reason this is its own unit.

AS.title: make A1 read contract-beta, the quantity ADR-0103 already chose
AS.commit: fix(doctor): gate A1 on contract-beta rather than the retired EXP-01 route
AS.note:
Read ADR-0103 in full before touching anything. It is the principal's own decision of 23 August 2026 and it is already ACCEPTED-PROVISIONAL.

THE DEFECT: `cli.py` still gates A1 on the EXP01_BETA regex, which reads EXP-01's history-mining measurement. EXP-01 WAS RETIRED -- its stopping rule fired because the interval would not narrow below plus-or-minus 0.05. So doctor is enforcing a route the project itself falsified, and ADR-0103 replaced. The decision moved and the code did not follow.

Make A1 read the CONTRACT-beta measurement instead, per ADR-0103. Human-beta is alignment, not a blocker, and A1 must not depend on it -- the principal is by design a weaker judge of output than the system, so a gate resting on his verdicts measures agreement with the weaker judge rather than correctness. That reasoning is his, recorded in the ADR, and it is the whole point of the change.

What you must NOT do: do not invent a new gate condition, do not relax the interval requirement, do not admit a proxy estimand. PROXY_ESTIMAND_KINDS exists precisely to keep critic_proxy_beta, mutation_proxy_beta and the repository-consequence lower bound OUT of the beta projection, and that separation stands. Contract-beta is not a proxy: a held-out contract the builder never saw is genuine ground truth, which is exactly why ADR-0103 chose it.

Depends on K01 because a contract that the dispatch could reach is not held out, and a contract-beta measured against a reachable contract measures nothing.

The test must fail if A1 ever passes without an interval, and must fail if it passes on a proxy estimand.

AT.title: recognise a signed verdict as authenticated so human-beta can be measured without the principal being a gate
AT.commit: feat(projection): admit ssh-signed verdicts as authenticated
AT.note:
MEASURED 24 August 2026. `_verdict_auth_status` in projection.py recognises exactly two vias: 'phone_webauthn' maps to authenticated but is REFUSED AT APPEND, so it is unreachable; 'cli' with a principal maps to declared_principal, which `admits_human_beta_row` correctly refuses. The consequence is that human-verdict beta has NO admissible row and is structurally unmeasurable -- see the strict xfail in tests/test_verdict_supply.py.

CB1 already built the missing channel: scripts/sign_verdict.py derives the principal from an ssh signature via `ssh-keygen -Y find-principals`, never from a caller-supplied field. It landed in c45cb9a. Nothing connected it to the projection. This unit connects it.

Why declared_principal must STAY refused: a local agent process can write a syntactically valid declared-principal verdict, so admitting it would let the system fabricate the ground truth used to measure its own error rate. That is the exact self-deception this project exists to detect. Do not relax it. The repair is to build the honest channel, not to widen the dishonest one.

A signature verifies only if the public key is in an allowed-signers file the repository does not control, and verification must be reproducible years later by a third party from a clone alone. If only we can verify it, we could have fabricated it.

This does NOT make the principal a gate. Under ADR-0103 human-beta is alignment rather than a blocker; this unit means that when verdicts ARE signed they count, and when there are none nothing is blocked.

AU.title: narrow the cursor lock to startup so Cursor capacity is usable
AU.commit: fix(dispatch): hold the cursor lock over startup, not the whole run
AU.note:
MEASURED 24 August 2026. The principal reports Cursor quota at 4% used while Claude and Codex are saturated, and this is why.

`scripts/dispatch.py` wraps the ENTIRE cursor-composer run in ExclusiveFileLock(DEFAULT_CURSOR_LOCK) for the full leash. With a 3600s leash that means one cursor dispatch per hour: extras block their whole leash and then fail with 'cursor-agent lock held'. Three units burned an hour each that way on 24 Aug, and build_driver.py had to add CURSOR_CONCURRENCY = 1 to stop the driver wasting slots on dispatches that could never start.

WHAT THE LOCK PROTECTS, measured: the comment says two cursor-agent processes race `~/.cursor/cli-config.json`. That file contains NO credentials -- only preferences (approvalMode, display, permissions, sandbox, version). Its mtime on 24 Aug was 21 Aug 22:24, THREE DAYS STALE, across dozens of cursor dispatches. So ordinary runs do not write it at all; it is written only when a setting changes.

So the lock's EXISTENCE is defensible and its SCOPE is not: an hour-long exclusive hold protects a file written perhaps weekly, and it costs almost all of a paid quota.

Narrow it to the window where contention is real -- process startup, when the config is read -- and release it once the child is running. Measure where the write actually happens before choosing the boundary; do not guess the number. If cursor-agent turns out to write the config on exit too, say so and cover both ends rather than pretending one is enough.

Then raise CURSOR_CONCURRENCY in .harness/build_driver.py to match what the narrowed lock genuinely allows, and say what you measured it to be.

DO NOT simply delete the lock. A corrupted cli-config.json would break every cursor dispatch at once, and the race is real even if rare. The test must prove two concurrent dispatches can run AND that the config survives them intact.

AV.title: read the cross-family verdict instead of discarding it
AV.commit: fix(driver): consume the review verdict and block retirement on a bad one
AV.note:
MEASURED 24 August 2026, and this is the most beta-adverse defect in the build.

The driver dispatches a cross-family review for every built unit -- a DIFFERENT MODEL FAMILY from the builder, which is the only genuinely different class of evidence in the whole pipeline -- writes the reviewer's output to `<uid>-verify.out`, and then NEVER READS IT. `state["verified"]` is read at build_driver.py:1138 and :1142 and initialised at :1082, and NOTHING WRITES A UNIT INTO IT. The 19 entries currently there came from a hand-run review on 23 Aug, not from the pipeline.

So every review is dispatched, billed against the principal's quota, and discarded. The system performs consilience and throws away the result. Per CONSILIENCE.md the whole project rests on convergence from a different class of facts being a TEST -- a test whose outcome is never read is not a test, and a unit marked done on the builder's say-so alone is exactly the echo this repository exists to refuse.

What to build: parse `<uid>-verify.out` for a structured verdict, record it in `state["verified"]` and in the TRAJECTORY, and make a unit's retirement depend on it. A SOUND verdict retires the unit. A verdict finding blocking defects must PREVENT retirement and put the unit back for repair with the findings attached.

Require the reviewer to emit a machine-readable verdict; do not regex prose for the word 'sound'. An unparseable verdict is NOT a pass -- fail closed, because the whole point is that the absence of evidence stopped being treated as evidence.

Evidence for how strict this should be: the one hand-run cross-family review of 19 units found 0 sound, 5 blocking and 68 surviving findings, and 14 of 19 carried a guard that could be deleted with the suite still green. Reviewed is not sound, and the pipeline currently cannot tell the difference.

Do NOT make the verdict advisory-only to keep throughput up. Throughput through an unmeasured filter is the thing being sold here, and it is worth less than nothing.

PRIORITY 25, set deliberately on 24 August 2026. This unit unblocks nothing, so ordering by downstream impact would dispatch it last. That is backwards: it does not release work, it makes every unit already released trustworthy. Until it lands, 'done' means one model said so.

AW.title: record loop-engineering as the bar for the orchestration layer, and say honestly what is left
AW.commit: research(bar): loop-engineering as the incumbent for the orchestration layer
AW.note:
